body:
I would say "is the logical time between physics ticks".

There are two things there:
* Firstly the physics delta pass is *not* real time, it is logical time. If you were to measure the wall clock time at each physics tick, it would bear no resemblence to the delta here.
* It's good practice to move from referring to physics ticks from frames to calling them ticks, in order to prevent confusion. Physics ticks are not frames. We did agree to standardize this a bit more for 4.x (there's a lot of things that still refer to physics frames in 3.x).

body:
Again, no the process delta is not a logical delta.

Frame delta is a measured delta between two points (often before SwapBuffers), and can be optionally modified by delta smoothing, to iron out variations.

Physics delta is not processed in real time, it is processed in logical steps, with the number of steps calculated based on the frame delta.

body:
This change is rather dubious imo.

Low performance is not *just* caused by CPU, perhaps more often is caused by GPU (and CPU is waiting), especially on integrated GPU. Or could be hard disk, waiting for network, etc. CPU limiting performance is more common in specific circumstances, like heavy physics simulations etc.

Might be better to stay non-specific, maybe say something like:

> [b]Note:[/b] [method _physics_process] may be called up to [member Engine.max_physics_steps_per_frame] times per (idle) frame. This step limit may be reached when the engine is suffering performance issues.
